Method of Attack: Sideloading malicious Windows DLLs into antivirus products to run code with high privileges and evade detection
Using Impacket Python kit to facilitate lateral movement and remote code execution via Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI)
Credential stealing by capturing password change events and writing them to a log file
Dropping a passive loader that activates based on hostname comparison
Using WinDivert packet sniffer for self-decryption and payload launching
Deploying backdoors PlugX and ShadowPad for data exfiltration
Impacted Systems: Windows OS systems running antivirus products from TrendMicro, Bitdefender, McAfee, Symantec, and Kaspersky
Attack Vector: Side-loading malicious DLLs into high-privilege antivirus processes
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious DLLs sideloaded into antivirus products
Log file at C:\Windows\Temp\Filter.log capturing password change events
Payload files named SNAC.log or bdch.tmp
